messages.text: What fee applies if I withdraw from a term deposit before maturity?

data.answer:
An administrative fee of 25 RON (or the equivalent of 5 EUR / 5 USD for foreign‑currency deposits) is deducted from the principal on early withdrawal, and all interest accrued since opening (or since the last renewal) is forfeited — the customer receives principal minus the fee [4].

Exception: no fee or interest forfeiture applies if the withdrawal is due to the death of the account holder (verified by the estate) or a court order; these exceptions require a branch visit and cannot be processed through the mobile app or call centre [2].

messages.text: What is the deposit guarantee coverage limit at Libra Bank?

data.answer:
The guarantee limit is 100,000 EUR equivalent per depositor, per bank — this applies regardless of currency, number of accounts or number of products (balances across accounts are added for the limit) [4].

Coverage is provided by the national Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund and applies to principal plus interest accrued up to the date of a bank default; for joint accounts each holder is covered up to 100,000 EUR equivalent on their share combined with their other deposits at Libra Bank [1][2].

messages.text: What is the withholding tax rate on deposit interest?

data.answer:
Withholding tax on deposit interest for individual customers is 10% of the gross interest; it is deducted automatically by Libra Bank at the moment interest is paid (at maturity for terms up to 12 months, or annually for longer terms) [1][4]. 

This 10% rate applies uniformly across RON, EUR and USD deposits and across the bank’s retail deposit products; withholding treatment for business (legal‑entity) accounts differs and is not covered here [2].

history.q: What is the minimum amount to open a standard term deposit?
history.a: Minimum opening amount for a standard term deposit is 1,000 RON (or the equivalent amount in EUR or USD) [1].

history.q: What fee applies if I withdraw from a term deposit before maturity?
history.a:
An administrative fee of 25 RON (or the equivalent of 5 EUR / 5 USD for foreign‑currency deposits) is deducted from the principal on early withdrawal, and all interest accrued since opening (or since the last renewal) is forfeited — the customer receives principal minus the fee [4].

Exception: no fee or interest forfeiture applies if the withdrawal is due to the death of the account holder (verified by the estate) or a court order; these exceptions require a branch visit and cannot be processed through the mobile app or call centre [2].

history.q: What is the deposit guarantee coverage limit at Libra Bank?
history.a:
The guarantee limit is 100,000 EUR equivalent per depositor, per bank — this applies regardless of currency, number of accounts or number of products (balances across accounts are added for the limit) [4].

Coverage is provided by the national Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund and applies to principal plus interest accrued up to the date of a bank default; for joint accounts each holder is covered up to 100,000 EUR equivalent on their share combined with their other deposits at Libra Bank [1][2].

history.q: What is the withholding tax rate on deposit interest?
history.a:
Withholding tax on deposit interest for individual customers is 10% of the gross interest; it is deducted automatically by Libra Bank at the moment interest is paid (at maturity for terms up to 12 months, or annually for longer terms) [1][4]. 

This 10% rate applies uniformly across RON, EUR and USD deposits and across the bank’s retail deposit products; withholding treatment for business (legal‑entity) accounts differs and is not covered here [2].

history.q: What is the current notice period for a notice savings account?
history.a:
The current notice period is 45 calendar days from the date the withdrawal request is submitted, regardless of the amount requested (policy effective 2026-01-15) [3].

There is no way to expedite or waive the 45-day notice; requests submitted before 2026-01-15 were honoured at the prior 30-day period. Once the notice period elapses, funds become available for transfer to the linked current account for 5 business days — if not withdrawn in that window the request expires and must be resubmitted [4][1].
